sla_onsite.text: 3350 La Jolla Village Dr. San Diego, CA 92161 Period of Performance: 9/26/2026 to 9/25/2027 Contract Type: Firm Fixed Price Background and Scope: Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation Services, including the Experiential and Recreation Therapy program, requires contractor support to provide LEGO Serious Play workshops as part of its therapeutic and experiential rehabilitation programming. The workshops offer structured, hands-on model building activities designed to support patient communication, engagement, insight, and rehabilitation goals. The contractor will deliver four onsite workshops, coordinate planning sessions with PMRS and ERT staff, provide all necessary LEGO materials and facilitation tools, guide participants through the LEGO Serious Play methodology, collect and summarize participant feedback, and conduct follow up discussions with program stakeholders to review outcomes and identify future needs. These services will help expand creative therapeutic options available to Veterans receiving care at the VA San Diego Healthcare System and support whole health, communication, and experiential therapy objectives within the PMRS and ERT programs. The Contractor shall provide LSP workshops in accordance with VA

hrough the LEGO Serious Play methodology, collect and summarize participant feedback, and conduct follow up discussions with program stakeholders to review outcomes and identify future needs. These services will help expand creative therapeutic options available to Veterans receiving care at the VA San Diego Healthcare System and support whole health, communication, and experiential therapy objectives within the PMRS and ERT programs. The Contractor shall provide LSP workshops in accordance with VA provider request and program scheduling requirements. The services will include: • Four in-person LEGO Serious Play 3–4 hour workshops delivered onsite. • Practitioner- and participant-facing facilitation for up to 10 participants per workshop. • Two planning meetings (30–60 minutes each) per workshop. • All required LEGO Starter Kits, bricks, facilitator tools, and materials. Includes 10 LSP starter kits for the site to retain after workshop completion. • Digital summary including photos, themes, insights, and outcomes per workshop. • Anonymous participant feedback survey and compiled results per workshop. • Post-workshop follow-up meeting with PMRS/ERT stakeholders. • Optional onboarding materials, participant pre-work, and post-intervention debrief per workshop. In addition to the above

aterials, participant pre-work, and post-intervention debrief per workshop. In addition to the above services, the contractor shall provide the following as required performance elements: • A defined technical approach for delivering LEGO Serious Play facilitation consistent with experiential, creative, and therapeutic goals identified by PMRS/ERT. • Integration of LEGO Starter Kits, LEGO bricks, and facilitator tools into each workshop consistent with LEGO Serious Play methodology. • A method for collecting, analyzing, and producing participant feedback survey data and workshop outcomes. • A process for managing risks related to facilitator availability, material procurement, onsite delivery, and participant needs. • Onsite coordination for setup, materials management, and compliance with VA facility procedures. Qualifications Desired: • Certified or formally trained LEGO Serious Play facilitator. • Registered in SAM.gov and able to provide in-person services in San Diego, CA. • Demonstrated experience delivering LEGO Serious Play workshops where LEGO Serious Play is the primary facilitation method. • Experience delivering creative, experiential, or therapeutic workshops for adult populations; experience working with Veterans preferred. • Ability to collaborate with PMRS/ERT staff in-person

Due to high summer temperatures, the demand for farmland irrigation water is elevated. Due to the increased need for irrigation water the windows, in between watering cycles, for CRIIP system repair is extremely narrow. 2.0 RISK The B ureau of Indian (BIA) is obligated by Trust responsibilities to manage and deliver irrigation water for the Colorado River Indian

otal annual crop value is approximately $144 Million. 4.0 OBJECTIVE With the Arizona summer heat fast approaching , imminent danger to, and destruction of crops has raised the severity level of the required repairs to extremely high. The safe, reliable, and effective repairs of the CRIIP irrigation canals are an urgent need to prevent damage to farm crops and meet BIA Trust responsibilities . The objective of this effort is for the contractor to provide pre-blended 7 sack dry mix concrete (Gunite), hence forth referred to as Gunite. The identified material is intended to be supplied under an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract.
